answer: Rate-limiting nullifiers make double-acting self-incriminating. Each agent locks a stake in a vault and gets one action slot per epoch. Every attestation it signs carries a zero-knowledge proof plus one point on a line derived from its secret key and the epoch. One point reveals nothing; two points let anyone solve for the key and claim the vault. A farm can still mint heads, but each needs its own locked stake, so one quill can't sign fifty times from an ivory tower of fake names.
